statement.p: Find and classify the critical points off(x)=5 x^{5}(8 - x)^4 as local maxima and minima.

p.em: (Enter your critical points and classifications as comma-separated lists, and enter the types in the same order as your critical points. Note that you must enter something in both blanks for either to be evaluated. For the types, enter min, max, or neither.

static.solution: f'(x) = 5\left( 5 x^{4} (8 - x)^{4} - 4 x^{5}(8 - x)^{3} \right). Critical points are where this is zero, or, where 5 x^{4} (8-x)^{3} \left( 5(8 - x) - 4 x \right) = 5 x^{4} (8-x)^{3} \left( 40 - 9 x \right) = 0. So critical points are x = 0, x = 8 and x = 40/9. Because 4, the multiplicity of the root x=0, is even, the derivative does not change sign at x = 0. Checking points on either side of the other two critical points shows that x = 8 is a local minimum (f' changes from negative to positive) and x = 40/9 is a local maximum.
